title: Further refinements of Euler-Mahonian statistics for multipermutations
summary: Permutation statistics constitute a classical subject of enumerative combinatorics. In her study of the genus zeta function, Denert discovered a new Mahonian statistic for permutations, which is called the Denert's statistic ({\bf $\den$}) by Foata and Zeilberger. As natural extensions of the $r$-descent number ({\bf $r\des$}) and the $r$-major index ({\bf $r\maj$}) introduced by Rawlings, Liu introduced the $g$-gap $\ell$-level descent number ({\bf $g\des_{\ell}$}) and the $g$-gap $\ell$-level major index ({\bf $g\maj_{\ell}$}) for permutations.
